forecast-period.text: A low pressure system over Western Australian will move over South Australia today, with an associated trough. A ridge of high pressure will follow and persist into early next week. A cold front clips the southeast on Sunday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Scattered showers, tending isolated about the far northeast and western coasts. Thunderstorms possible across most districts, becoming more likely in the north. Maximum temperature near to below average, grading to above average in the northeast. Southeast to northeasterly winds tending northwesterly ahead of a fresh west to southwesterly change extending throughout by evening.

Isolated showers about southern agricultural area and western coasts, possibly extending into the northern agricultural areas and southern pastorals. Isolated thunderstorms about the north. Maximum temperature below average, grading to above average in the northeast. South to southwesterly winds, freshening during the afternoon.

Isolated showers about southern agricultural area and western coasts, most likely about windward coasts and ranges. Showers and thunderstorms developing about the northwest. Maximum temperatures below average statewide. Southwest to southeasterly winds, fresh at times about the coast.

text.p: Light morning showers about windward coasts and ranges. Showers and thunderstorms about the northwest. Maximum temperatures below average statewide. South to southeasterly winds, fresh at times about the coast. South to southeasterly winds fresh at times about the northeast and the coast.
Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Monday: 2 to 10 mm increasing to 10 to 20 mm west of about Ceduna, with isolated falls of 20 to 40 mm with thunderstorms in the west.
